description: FO 1.0 Green Cell corpus (22 actions) in Appendix B chronological order. Diplomacy bands/styles drawn from Green_Cell_Diplomatic_Hierarchy_Assessment_Moves_1_2; Instrument of Power assigned so the full PLI track set (Macro, Diplomacy, Information, NI, Glasl) is exercised. Notional submission_month spacing mirrors the Blue FO quarterly demo.
source_order: Fractured Order Interim Report V4.10.2 Appendix B — Move 1 Actions in Sequence, then Move 2 Actions in Sequence

diplomacy.rationale: EU used consultations to clarify alignment options on supply-chain security before committing to harder pressure.

actions.title: Meeting with U.S., EU, Japan, and ROK

diplomacy.rationale: France convened partners on supply-chain coordination while preserving French/EU agency rather than organizing coercive pressure.
ROK backed allied critical-minerals coordination without direct coercion of the PRC.
Compact builds a resource-security framework and aligns partners around resilience; economic delivery rides on bilateral diplomacy.

macro.rule_citation: Tie-break: allied joint purchasing / finance facility for critical minerals is L6 I6.05 (partner-support finance), not domestic L7 capacity
citations: Minerals Security Partnership (MSP) joint offtake and financing model
EU Critical Raw Materials Act external partnership instruments
macro.precedent_rationale: Partner mineral-security compacts exist and have been used, but a Korea-centered multi-party offtake facility at this scope remains only partially proven

modifier_rationales.funding_available: Compact text commits financing envelopes for offtake and processing
modifier_rationales.partners_committed: Named partner governments join the compact
modifier_rationales.timeline_mismatch: Mine and processing lead times exceed a single move horizon
modifier_rationales.multi_authority_coordination: Requires trade, finance, and industry ministries across partners

macro.fit_rationale: Diversifying mineral supply is a core Reframing mechanism for ROK economic security

actions.title: Building up new economic order (multilateral dialogue)

diplomacy.rationale: Japan used dialogue to frame supply-chain security and economic-order questions without coercive exclusion.
ASEAN convened capacity diversification while preserving openness and avoiding binary bloc choice.

macro.rule_citation: Overseas connectivity / processing capacity financing for minerals diversification is L6 I6.04, not domestic L7
citations: ASEAN Minerals Cooperation Action Plan instruments
World Bank / ADB critical minerals project finance precedents
macro.precedent_rationale: Regional minerals-capacity finance has precedents, but ASEAN-wide diversification packages at FO scale are only partially exercised

modifier_rationales.partners_committed: ASEAN members and dialogue partners join the initiative
modifier_rationales.timeline_mismatch: Processing capacity build exceeds move horizon
modifier_rationales.multi_authority_coordination: Requires ASEAN secretariat plus national mining/finance ministries

macro.fit_rationale: Diversification and autonomy align with Asia-Pacific Reframing without forcing confrontation

diplomacy.rationale: Extraordinary summit established an internal European position before external coordination with Blue or pressure on Red.

actions.title: U.S.-ROK tech / energy / defense industry treaty

diplomacy.rationale: Treaty deepened bilateral strategic-economic alignment across tech, energy, and defense industry without direct sanctions.
Built biotech and pharmaceutical resilience through bilateral cooperation rather than coercive exclusion.
ROK advanced defense/energy cooperation with France/EU as structured alignment, not public pressure signaling.
France sought influence through Global South outreach and alternative offerings rather than adversary-facing pressure.

info.summary: France launches a Global South partnership outreach campaign framing Europe as a rules-based alternative for technology, development, and climate cooperation.
info.audiences: Global South elites and publics; EU domestic audiences; PRC narrative organs watching for neo-colonial framing.
info.narratives: Blue/Green: partnership and autonomy. Red: Western competition for influence. Local: opportunity vs. pressure to choose.
info.second_order_effects: May raise expectations for financing that outrun delivery; can dilute Blue pressure coalitions if framed as non-alignment.
info.sme_questions: Which Global South capitals are priority, and does White Cell treat this as competing with or complementing Blue inducements?
info.suggested_sme_edits: Name priority countries and concrete offer packages; clarify attribution and media channels.

actions.title: EU-UK global tech summit + communications line

diplomacy.rationale: Positioned Europe/UK as a rules-based technology actor via public-facing convening and a standing communications channel.
Built allied industrial capacity through structured transatlantic alignment rather than public adversary signaling.

macro.rule_citation: Domestic/allied industrial subsidy and co-production incentives for defense base are L7 I7.01 (industrial policy), with foreign deployment facets secondary
citations: EU European Defence Fund / ASAP instruments
U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council defense-industrial workstreams
NATO DIANA / defence innovation cooperative finance
macro.precedent_rationale: Transatlantic defense-industrial finance tools exist but a fully integrated base package at this scope is only partially proven

modifier_rationales.funding_available: Industrial base package includes budgeted co-investment
modifier_rationales.partners_committed: EU and U.S. industrial partners named
modifier_rationales.timeline_mismatch: Defense industrial ramp spans multiple years
modifier_rationales.multi_authority_coordination: Requires defense, competition, and finance authorities on both sides

macro.fit_rationale: Supports Stabilization via capacity and alliance management; only partially a Reframing play

diplomacy.rationale: Built long-term regional capacity and influence through an institutional education/S&T platform.

info.summary: ASEAN stands up a SEAMEO biotech center of excellence to build regional scientific capacity and soft-power networks over a multi-year horizon.
info.audiences: Southeast Asian students and researchers; national education ministries; industry R&D communities; competing PRC education diplomacy channels.
info.narratives: Green: inclusive regional capacity. Blue: complementary Indo-Pacific knowledge networks. Red: Western-aligned soft power.
info.second_order_effects: Low coerciveness but slow payoff; may shape talent pipelines and standards communities without moving Glasl stage.
info.sme_questions: Does White Cell credit near-term sentiment effects, or only long-horizon human-capital effects?
info.suggested_sme_edits: Specify host country, funding share, and curriculum focus areas.

diplomacy.rationale: Used joint-exercise signaling to communicate resolve and coordinate pressure with partners.
Protected maritime and semiconductor flows through partner coordination among FR/JP/ROK.

actions.title: SWAP arrangements to stabilize the won

diplomacy.rationale: Used bilateral financial diplomacy to manage market shock via swap-line consultation.

macro.rule_citation: Bilateral partner-support currency swap / central-bank liquidity line is L6 I6.06 (rule 4), not domestic FX intervention L5
citations: Bank of Korea-Federal Reserve dollar liquidity swap line (activated 2020)
BOK bilateral swap network with ASEAN+3 partners
macro.precedent_rationale: ROK has repeatedly exercised bilateral and plurilateral swap authorities for won/dollar liquidity support

modifier_rationales.funding_available: Swap line size is authorized and drawable
modifier_rationales.partners_committed: Counterparty central bank agrees to the arrangement
modifier_rationales.multi_authority_coordination: Requires MOF and central bank coordination with partner authorities

macro.fit_rationale: Stabilizing financial conditions preserves room for Reframing industrial strategy under stress

diplomacy.rationale: Japan organized partner alignment explicitly around pressure on China rather than exploratory consultation.

actions.title: Ukraine EU accession / Turkey talks resume

diplomacy.rationale: Expanded institutional access to minerals, markets, and production capacity through accession and resumed Turkey talks.
Promoted non-PRC telecom alternatives through regional commercial-diplomatic alignment.

macro.rule_citation: Preferential market access / export promotion for trusted telecom vendors is L1 I1.05 (preferential trade access), not L2 entity listing
citations: Trusted vendor / clean network preferential procurement programs
CPTPP digital and telecom market-access schedules
macro.precedent_rationale: Preferential trusted-vendor trade promotion exists, but a region-wide 2030 expo package at FO scope is only partially proven

modifier_rationales.funding_available: Expo and export-credit support are budgeted
modifier_rationales.partners_committed: ASEAN hosts and vendor governments participate
modifier_rationales.timeline_mismatch: Vendor displacement and network rip-and-replace lag the move

macro.fit_rationale: Building alternative telecom supply is a direct Reframing mechanism

diplomacy.rationale: Public messaging used to contain spillover risk and shape perceptions around North Korea escalation.

info.summary: ROK issues a public warning statement on North Korea risk, aiming to deter spillover and shape allied and domestic perceptions during heightened regional tension.
info.audiences: ROK domestic public; DPRK leadership; U.S./Japan allies; PRC observers; regional markets.
info.narratives: ROK: responsible deterrence and crisis management. DPRK: hostile encirclement. PRC: regional instability driven by U.S. allies.
info.second_order_effects: Can raise Glasl stage via public prestige contest; may reassure or alarm markets depending on tone and allied echo.
info.sme_questions: Is the statement coordinated with Blue/Japan, and does White Cell treat DPRK and PRC audiences as joint or separate?
info.suggested_sme_edits: Capture exact wording, channel (presidential vs MOFAT), and allied co-signing.

diplomacy.rationale: Shifted toward harder dependency-reduction via sanctions and investment stoppage communicated as strategic pressure.

macro.rule_citation: Country-specific punitive sanctions are L4 I4.01; outbound investment stoppage rides as secondary I3.02 per split-at-intake practice
citations: EU restrictive measures framework (CFSP sanctions regulations)
France implementation of EU Russia sanctions packages (2022-2025)
EU outbound investment monitoring / screening initiatives
macro.precedent_rationale: France/EU have repeatedly exercised targeted sanctions and investment restrictions against strategic rivals

modifier_rationales.partners_committed: EU-level restrictive measures imply partner coordination
modifier_rationales.multi_authority_coordination: Requires foreign ministry, finance, and investment-screening authorities

macro.fit_rationale: Hard coercive dependency cuts conflict with Stabilization's preference for consultation-first coalition management
